# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue with his heart.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences food texture sensitivities and is selective with what he eats due to texture issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient suffers from hypotonia and is very stiff at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may experience developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had glue ear, which was diagnosed after several instances of ear infections.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia, which affects how he sees distant objects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel, and require regular dental check-ups.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to achieve milestones compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient takes longer to achieve milestones compared to peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had delayed fontanelle closure.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider referral for a skeletal review to monitor for spinal and hip issues
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delay and learning difficulties
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which affects his ability to focus on distant objects, and has suspected hearing impairment, particularly in noisy environments.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint, which affects his ability to focus on distant objects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve issue in his heart and requires regular check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation issues sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and speech delay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have developmental delay and learning difficulties.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has fluid in his ear and is waiting to see how it gets cleared up.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits very close to the TV or when reading books, and his parents are worried it might affect his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger than usual front teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have large front teeth, weak enamel, and other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is working on speech delay with therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech delay and is working on it with therapy.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth and enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor the patient's hearing and address any concerns.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and address any concerns.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition and adjust treatment as needed.
* Speech therapy to continue working on the patient's speech delay.
* Occupational therapy to help the patient with daily living skills and fine motor development.
* Physiotherapy to help the patient with muscle tone and gross motor development.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired easily and can't keep up with others when playing, suggesting possible cardiac issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had feeding difficulties as a baby, described as a poor feeder, but this has improved.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is described as clumsy and less coordinated than other kids his age, suggesting possible neurological issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks for things to be repeated because he didn't catch them the first time, indicating hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has trouble seeing things up close, diagnosed as hypermetropia.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to go to the dentist a lot because of some issues they're monitoring.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has speech difficulties and is not talking as much as he should be at his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor dental issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to check for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to check for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and address difficulties.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has heart concerns that require regular monitoring and check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is extremely particular about the texture of foods and will often refuse to eat certain things because of how they feel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues, appearing less steady on his feet compared to peers, and has complained about things looking blurry sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets overwhelmed in crowded or noisy areas, suggesting some sensitivity with his hearing, and has dental health issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss, and many children have required multiple aeration tube insertions to relieve pressure inside the ear.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains that things look blurry sometimes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has dental health issues, with frequent visits to the dentist for various problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination issues and undescended testes that the medical team is still looking into.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and address dental health issues
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess for vision problems such as astigmatism or squint
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review, including X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull, to assess for skeletal anomalies
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to address coordination and developmental issues
* Regular monitoring for tethered cord, particularly if sacral dimple is present

Parent: Our daughter has mentioned struggling to see the board at school, especially when the teacher writes in small letters or uses certain colors. We're concerned this might affect her learning if not addressed properly.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: She complains about tooth sensitivity whenever she eats cold foods like ice cream or frozen yogurt. It's been an issue for a while now.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes, our pediatrician recommended regular heart check-ups due to a familial history of heart conditions. So far everything has looked okay.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).

Parent: Our daughter was diagnosed with hip dysplasia and delayed fontanelle closure. Both conditions require monitoring and have implications for her mobility and skull development. Regular appointments with specialists help manage these conditions effectively.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a familial history of heart conditions and undergoes regular heart check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky with food textures and has a limited diet, avoiding certain foods like mashed potatoes or overcooked vegetables.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a tethered cord issue that was identified during early developmental checks and is monitored closely.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear recently, which caused discomfort and affected her balance.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles to see the board at school, especially with small letters or certain colors, and may have vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains about tooth sensitivity when eating cold foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, and some have large front teeth or other dental concerns.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision problems may affect her learning if not addressed properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, learning difficulties, and behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hip dysplasia and delayed fontanelle closure, which require monitoring and have implications for her mobility and skull development.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as an unusual structure of their spinal bones, short fingers, or curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth sensitivity and enamel weakness
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss
* Eyesight review to assess vision problems and provide corrective measures
* Cardiac review to monitor for heart conditions
* Referral for a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor for skeletal anomalies
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support development and address any delays or difficulties.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, she has this habit of squinting whenever she looks at things, even if they're not that far away. It's like her eyes get tired easily or something. I've been worried it might affect her learning or playing.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes... the TV volume always needs to be turned up really high for her to hear it properly. I'm constantly telling her to turn it down because it's too loud for me, but she insists it's not loud enough for her. It worries me that maybe there's a problem with her hearing.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Her teeth... they break or chip so easily! Just last week， she chipped a tooth while eating a sandwich. The dentist says it's because they're weak or something. I'm trying to get her to take better care of them‚ but accidents still happen.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's a septal defect... we found out during one of the routine check-ups when she was younger. The doctor said it's not life-threatening but needs monitoring. So‚ we go back regularly to make sure everything stays okay.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain‚ nerves‚ muscle tone‚ fits).
Parent: She has hypotonia... her muscles seem too relaxed sometimes. When she was smaller‚ it was more noticeable‚ but now it's more about how she moves and plays rather than anything alarming. Still‚ I worry about it affecting her coordination or balance.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding‚ stomach‚ bowel).
Parent: Feeding was a nightmare when she was a baby. She wouldn't latch on properly and would spit up a lot. Thankfully‚ that phase passed‚ and now she eats normally. But those early months were incredibly stressful.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Well... apart from what I mentioned‚ there's also the speech delay. She started talking later than her peers‚ and even now‚ she sometimes struggles to find the right words. And then there's the issue with her fontanelle not closing properly... it's been a concern since birth‚ and we're waiting to see if it corrects itself over time.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected for her age during physical activity, which is monitored closely with her pediatrician.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, with some requiring surgery.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has feeding challenges with strong aversions to certain foods, requiring close work with a nutritionist to ensure balanced meals.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired quickly during physical activity, which could be related to her overall health or a specific issue to be explored further with a specialist.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome experience seizures, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear in the past, which was treated with antibiotics and has not recurred.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, corrected with glasses, which has improved her ability to see distant objects.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, requiring careful management of her diet to avoid hard foods.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, there can be other dental concerns including weak enamel, making regular dental check-ups important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, with many attending mainstream primary school but possibly requiring special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans for secondary education.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay and behavioural differences, including autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, including an unusual structure of spinal bones, short fingers, and curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent issues.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially given the history of glue ear.
* Continued monitoring of vision to adjust glasses prescription as needed.
* Ongoing management of feeding challenges and dietary aversions.
* Close monitoring of heart health, given the potential for cardiac issues in KBG syndrome.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy as needed to support overall development and address specific challenges.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient often asks to have things repeated because he didn't quite catch what was said, suggesting hearing difficulties.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient rubs his eyes often, especially when trying to focus, suggesting vision problems.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen, and careful brushing is very important, with regular dental check-ups recommended.

* Monitoring of growth velocity, with referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
